challenged_assumptions.assumption: The embryo-held-out kill test proved that a coordinate head retrained on 199 videos is worse than the public head.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful:
The comparator is asymmetric. The public x138 head was trained on 20 movies that include both embryos, so in each 'embryo-held-out' direction it is in-embryo while the new head is out-of-embryo. Evidence that the test is conservative rather than decisive:
- P trained on 44b6 only tied the public head on 6bba (+0.19%) even though the public head had seen 6bba;
- on equal exposure (leak5 OOF) the new head is 19% (P) / 6.4% (Q, debiased) closer to GT.
The test is still real evidence against the 6bba->44b6 direction (+12% P, +6.3% Q). So the closure is 'unproven', not 'refuted': the LB is the only judge, and only through a blended head that cannot drift far from the public one.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: In x138 every node carries the head's refined float coordinates.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: Only the >= 0.965 peaks in `arr` pass through _v1284_refine. The LOWDET pool (peaks >= 0.3) is detected separately, multiplied by downsample and cast to int16. READMIT places nodes at peaks['vox'] from that pool, and GAPFILL uses the same pool. These nodes therefore sit on the 4-voxel (1.625 um) y/x grid, with no head shift, at exactly the contested track ends. On the 4 dummy clips that is 1,337 readmitted nodes out of 121,777.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: x138's flow-prior relink fully fixes the whole-frame-jump failure of the public post-processing.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: The flow prior compensates field motion inside the relink. However, x138 still applies OUTPUT_EDGE_MAX_UM = 14 on RAW distance before the relink, so frame pairs with a jump above about 10-14 um lose links whatever the flow says. On the public 0.942 stack, links on frames with >= 5 um shifts were missed 32% of the time after post-processing against 10% at the ILP stage. The effect is small on the train distribution (0.37% of links) but unknown on the hidden embryos.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Ultrack (the organisers' tracker) centroids could serve as a position oracle for the annotations, because the GT was likely made with ultrack plus proofreading.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful:
The team already measured this on the dorado movie (= the 44b6 recording, which the Ultrack sparse_zebrafish configuration uses with DS_LENGTH 521):
- GT -> Ultrack point median distance is 1.29 um;
- snapping our nodes to Ultrack points lowers the share of nodes within 4 um (0.927 -> 0.908).
So the 'ultrack-centroid snap' idea suggested by the royerlab configurations is closed by data, not by opinion.

hypotheses.title: Pass x138's READMIT / GAPFILL peaks through the V1284 head (and keep them float), so the ~1-4% of nodes at contested track ends stop sitting on the 1.625 um coarse grid
hypotheses.mechanism: In x138, `_v1284_refine` runs only on the >= 0.965 peaks `arr`. The LOWDET pool (peaks >= 0.3) comes from a second `_detect_cells_pooled` call, is multiplied by downsample and cast to int16. READMIT re-adds pool peaks >= 0.965 within 4 um of an open track end. GAPFILL bridges gaps with pool peaks >= 0.5. Both place nodes at the unrefined integer `vox`, whose y/x lies on the 4-voxel grid (1.625 um steps, +-0.81 um), with none of the head's learned shift (mean |shift| 0.74 um, -9.5% GT distance on the capture set). These nodes sit exactly where the head matters most: at open ends next to other cells, where the swap-type FN live (BRIEF: ~2,700 swap FN are node-position errors, matched at 4.4 um vs 1.8 um). This is a positions-only change: it does not lean on network confidence, the class of change that transferred from lab to LB (insertion: lab +0.0019 -> LB +0.001).

hypotheses.title: Apply the public V1284 head twice (second pass on trilinear features at the refined position, damped), validated out-of-sample on the ~179 videos the head never saw
hypotheses.mechanism: The V1284 head makes a single bounded step (< 2 um) from the integer peak, using 7 feature samples on the 1.625 um grid. After one pass the public head still leaves the fixed-pair mean GT distance at 1.525 um and the median at 1.35 um. The node is off by more than one grid step in many cases, while the trilinear feature gather (already in x138 for the transformer) can re-read features at the refined position. A cascaded or iterated regressor is the standard way to shrink the residual of a one-step keypoint head without training. The positions feed flow relink, readmit, gapfill and the safe divisions, which is why one pass was worth +0.007 on x138. Crucially, this needs NO new training: the public head is out-of-sample on the ~179 train videos outside its 20-movie training set. Those videos give an honest held-out estimate, the same kind of check the x138 author used (held-out-by-movie -10.4%). The in-sample trap does not apply to the head (only to the UNet features), and the UNet in-sample issue is identical for pass 1 and pass 2.
hypotheses.change: In the x138 module text (v1284_coordinate_refinement.py), add `sample_features_trilinear(feature, arr_float)`: the same 7 offsets (centre + 6 faces at +-1 voxel), gathered with the existing 8-corner trilinear code used by `index_features`. Then add `V1284_PASSES` (default 1 = byte-identical) and `V1284_DAMP` (default 1.0). Pass k: `x = bounded(head, (sample_features_trilinear(F, arr) - mean)/scale)`, `arr += DAMP * x / SPACING`. Keep the total |shift| <= 2 um; the existing raise is on total shift, so clip or scale it. Candidate settings: passes 2 with damping 0.5 or 1.0.

hypotheses.title: Re-open the 199-video head only as a 50/50 blend with the public head, behind a fair (exposure-matched) kill test
hypotheses.mechanism: The x138 author's own notes say head quality scales with training movies: a 4-movie head was +14.9% worse than the 20-movie head. Our 199-video head is 19% closer to GT than the public head at equal exposure (leak5 OOF), but it failed the embryo-held-out kill test, partly because it learns 6bba's z convention (+0.57 um shift). The test is asymmetric: the public comparator saw both embryos, and a single-embryo head is compared to it out-of-embryo. The 44b6-only head still tied the public head on 6bba (+0.19%), which suggests part of the 199-video gain is generalisable. A 50/50 average of the public and the embryo-debiased (Q) predictions halves any learned convention and keeps the public head's known-good LB behaviour. Averaging two regressors is the least risky way to take part of the extra accuracy.
